title: Effects of four workplace lighting technologies on perception, cognition and affective state

findings.antecedent: lighting condition (Fluorescent, LED 1, LED 2, LED 3)
findings.consequent: percent correct responses on pseudoisochromatic plates (Color Recognition Task 1)
findings.quote: Analysis of percent correct responses to the pseudoisochromatic plates did not reveal a difference as a function of lighting condition, F(3,69) = .21, p = .89, η² = .01.

findings.antecedent: lighting condition (Fluorescent, LED 1, LED 2, LED 3)
findings.consequent: color hue test time to completion (Color Recognition Task 2)
findings.mechanism: Increased color temperature with smaller pupil size and thus enhanced visual acuity; arousal's ability to enhance reaction times.
findings.quote: Analysis of the color hue test time to completion data revealed different completion times as a function of lighting condition, F(3,69) = 3.67, p = .02, η² = .14

findings.antecedent: LED 2 lighting (5448 K) relative to Fluorescent lighting (3345 K)
findings.consequent: color hue test completion time
findings.mechanism: Increased color temperature with smaller pupil size and thus enhanced visual acuity.
findings.quote: Relative to fluorescent, the LED 2 (marginally), t(23) = 1.88, p = .07, d = .38, ... showed faster completion times

findings.antecedent: LED 3 lighting (6029 K) relative to Fluorescent lighting (3345 K)
findings.consequent: color hue test completion time
findings.mechanism: Increased color temperature with smaller pupil size and thus enhanced visual acuity.
findings.quote: Relative to fluorescent, ... and LED 3 conditions, t(23) = 3.02, p < .01, d = .62, showed faster completion times

findings.antecedent: LED 3 lighting (6029 K) relative to LED 1 lighting (4175 K)
findings.consequent: color hue test completion time
findings.mechanism: Increased color temperature with smaller pupil size and thus enhanced visual acuity.
findings.quote: Further, the LED 3 condition showed marginally faster completion times relative to the LED 1 condition, t(23) = 1.94, p = .07, d = .40.

findings.antecedent: lighting condition (Fluorescent, LED 1, LED 2, LED 3)
findings.consequent: error rates on color hue test
findings.quote: Error rates on this task, however, did not vary as a function of lighting condition, F(3,69) = 1.26, p = .29, η² = .05.

findings.antecedent: lighting condition (Fluorescent, LED 1, LED 2, LED 3)
findings.consequent: error rates on Snellen Eye Chart (Visual Acuity Task 1)
findings.quote: Analysis of error rates on the Snellen Eye Chart did not reveal a difference as a function of lighting condition, F(3,69) = 1.04, p = .38, η² = .04.

findings.antecedent: lighting condition (Fluorescent, LED 1, LED 2, LED 3)
findings.consequent: depression (POMS difference score)
findings.mechanism: Higher color temperatures can mitigate Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD) and increase positive mood.
findings.quote: For depression, there was a main effect of lighting condition, F(3,69) = 4.64, p < .01, η² = .17, with overall higher difference scores at the lower color temperatures

findings.antecedent: Fluorescent lighting (3345 K) relative to LED 2 lighting (5448 K)
findings.consequent: depression (POMS difference score)
findings.mechanism: Higher color temperatures can mitigate Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD).
findings.quote: specifically, there was significantly higher rated depression in the fluorescent relative to the LED 2 condition (marginally), t(23) = 2.02, p = .05, d = .41

findings.antecedent: Fluorescent lighting (3345 K) relative to LED 3 lighting (6029 K)
findings.consequent: depression (POMS difference score)
findings.mechanism: Higher color temperatures can mitigate Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD).
findings.quote: and the LED 3 condition, t(23) = 2.6, p < .05, d = .53.

findings.antecedent: LED 1 lighting (4175 K) relative to LED 3 lighting (6029 K)
findings.consequent: depression (POMS difference score)
findings.mechanism: Higher color temperatures can mitigate Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD).
findings.quote: Further, there was lower rated depression in the LED 3 condition relative to the LED 1 condition, t(23) = 3.56, p < .01, d = .73.

findings.antecedent: lighting condition (Fluorescent, LED 1, LED 2, LED 3)
findings.consequent: vigor/activity (POMS difference score)
findings.mechanism: Higher color temperatures produced an increase in vigor/activity.
findings.quote: For vigor/activity, there was a main effect of lighting condition, F(3,69) = 3.23, p < .05, η² = .12, with overall lower difference scores at the lower color temperatures

findings.antecedent: Fluorescent lighting (3345 K) relative to LED 3 lighting (6029 K)
findings.consequent: vigor/activity (POMS difference score)
findings.mechanism: Higher color temperatures produced an increase in vigor/activity.
findings.quote: specifically, there was significantly lower rated vigor/activity in the fluorescent relative to the LED 3 condition, t(23) = 2.92, p < .01, d = .60

findings.antecedent: LED 1 lighting (4175 K) relative to LED 3 lighting (6029 K)
findings.consequent: vigor/activity (POMS difference score)
findings.mechanism: Higher color temperatures produced an increase in vigor/activity.
findings.quote: and in the LED 1 relative to the LED 3 condition, t(23) = 2.39, p < .05, d = .49.

findings.antecedent: lighting condition (Fluorescent, LED 1, LED 2, LED 3)
findings.consequent: fatigue (POMS difference score)
findings.mechanism: Higher color temperatures decreased fatigue scores.
findings.quote: Finally, for fatigue, there was also a main effect of lighting condition, F(3, 69) = 3.10, p < .05, η² = .12

findings.antecedent: Fluorescent lighting (3345 K) relative to LED 2 lighting (5448 K)
findings.consequent: fatigue (POMS difference score)
findings.mechanism: Higher color temperatures decreased fatigue scores.
findings.quote: specifically, there was significantly higher rated fatigue in the fluorescent relative to the LED 2 condition, t(23) = 2.14, p < .05, d = .44

findings.consequent: fatigue (POMS difference score)
findings.mechanism: Higher color temperatures decreased fatigue scores.
findings.quote: and the LED 3 condition, t(23) = 2.88, p < .01, d = .59.

findings.antecedent: LED 1 lighting (4175 K) relative to LED 3 lighting (6029 K)
findings.consequent: fatigue (POMS difference score)
findings.mechanism: Higher color temperatures decreased fatigue scores.
findings.quote: Further, the LED 3 condition showed lower fatigue ratings relative to the LED 1 condition, t(23) = 1.82, p = .08, d = .37.

findings.antecedent: lighting condition (Fluorescent, LED 1, LED 2, LED 3)
findings.consequent: accuracy on auditory sequence monitoring task (Cognitive Task 1)
findings.quote: As expected, accuracy was overall high for this task, and did not vary as a function of lighting condition, F(3,60) = .307, p > .05, η² = .02.

findings.consequent: accuracy on verbal event planning task (Cognitive Task 2)
findings.quote: demonstrated that accuracy did not vary significantly as a function of lighting condition, F(3,69) = 1.89, p > .05, η² = .08.

findings.consequent: reaction time on verbal event planning task

findings.quote: Reaction time to correctly answered trials, however, improved in a generally linear manner as a function of increasing color temperature, F(3,69) = 6.36, p < .01, η² = .22.

findings.consequent: reaction time on spatial map study task

findings.consequent: reaction time on spatial map study task

findings.antecedent: reduced depression ratings (LED 3 vs Fluorescent)
findings.consequent: reaction times on Cognitive Task 2 (verbal event task)
findings.mechanism: Positive moods can benefit memory and other cognitive tasks.
findings.quote: those who showed reduced depression ratings in the LED 3 condition relative to fluorescent also tended to show faster reaction times in LED 3 relative to fluorescent, β = 57.32, t(23) = 2.35, p = .03, R2 = .19.

findings.antecedent: reduced depression ratings (LED 3 vs Fluorescent)
findings.consequent: reaction times on Cognitive Task 3 (spatial map task)
findings.mechanism: Positive moods can benefit memory and other cognitive tasks.
findings.quote: The same pattern was found with Cognitive Task 3, β = 55.13, t(23) = 2.49, p = .02, R2 = .23.

findings.antecedent: increased vigor/activity ratings (LED 3 vs Fluorescent)
findings.consequent: reaction times on Cognitive Task 2 (verbal event task)
findings.mechanism: Increased arousal will translate to enhanced cognitive task performance.
findings.quote: For vigor/activity ratings, we found that those who showed increased vigor/activity ratings in the LED 3 condition relative to fluorescent also tended to show faster reaction times during Cognitive Task 2 in LED 3 relative to fluorescent (marginally), β = -41.72, t(23) = 1.89, p = .07, R2 = .21.

findings.antecedent: increased vigor/activity ratings (LED 3 vs Fluorescent)
findings.consequent: reaction times on Cognitive Task 3 (spatial map task)
findings.mechanism: Increased arousal will translate to enhanced cognitive task performance.
findings.quote: The same trend was found with Cognitive Task 3, but did not reach significance, β = −31.95, t(23) = 1.32, p = .20, R2 = .13.

findings.mechanism: Decreased fatigue will translate to enhanced cognitive task performance.
findings.quote: Finally, for fatigue ratings, we found that those who showed decreased fatigue ratings in the LED 3 condition relative to fluorescent also tended to show faster reaction times during Cognitive Task 2 in LED 3 relative to fluorescent, β = 114.12, t(23) = 2.93, p < .01, R2 = .28.

stimuli.description: A climate-controlled Tent Expandable Modular Personnel (TEMPER) military shelter (640 sq. ft.) equipped with one of four lighting technologies: Fluorescent (3345 K), LED 1 (4175 K), LED 2 (5448 K), LED 3 (6029 K).

tables.description: Mean tested color temperature of each lighting technology, in degrees Kelvin.

Mean and standard deviation for percent correct responses (Color Recognition Task 1), number of errors and completion times (Color Recognition Task 2), and error rates (Visual Acuity Task 1) for the three visual perception tasks and each of the four lighting conditions.
Mean and standard deviation composite mood difference (post-pre) scores for the depression, vigor/activity, and fatigue subscales of the POMS, for each of the four lighting conditions.
Mean and standard deviation accuracy and reaction times (RT in milliseconds) from each of the two primary cognitive tasks, and each of the four lighting conditions.

limitations: Participants may have developed preferences for particular lighting types from daily experiences, and these preexisting preferences could have influenced the results.
